newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo can succeed without merger - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Volvo can succeed without merger - CEO.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Monday it can succeed without merging with another company, although cooperation with Japan's Mitsubishi should continue.
New Chief Executive Officer Leif Johansson said in an interview with Swedish daily Svenska Dagbladet that there were more synergies within the Volvo corporation to deal with.
"There are considerable synergies between our various business areas and within them," he said when asked if Volvo could survive future challenges without entering into a major alliance.

Johansson said there were no concrete projects on the table for cooperation with Mitsubishi but added: "I can think of common points of interest between (construction equipment unit) VCE and Mitsubishi. That would be interesting," he said.
Johansson said Volvo planned to increase investments in eastern Europe.
"I believe that Volvo has good possibilities in a relatively short time period to do significant business in eastern Europe," Johansson told the newspaper.
The newspaper quoted him as saying he was focusing on eastern Europe and carried over experience from working on those markets from his time as head of appliance maker AB Electrolux.
Johansson took over has head of Volvo from Electrolux earlier this year.
"In the short term (eastern European) markets will be significantly more profitable than Asia," Svenska Dagbladet quoted him as saying.
"Today our turnover in eastern Europe is nearly 2.8 billion crowns. This number will increase two- or three-fold in five years," he told the newspaper.
Asked how much money Volvo Cars would be making in the future, Johansson told the newspaper the company's goal was an operating margin of five to seven percent over a business cycle.
"We are not there yet, but we have good products in the pipeline," he told Svenska Dagbladet.
